Distribution utilities allocate limited budgets among reinforcement, distributed energy resources, storage, and automation. This optimizer study represents those choices with a SimBench-derived portfolio proxy, not action-aligned expansion decisions. CARS-MODE combines binary multi-objective differential evolution, adaptive parameters and mutation strategies, budget repair, and crowding. A 2940-run rerun exactly reproduces the archived sampled-bound hypervolumes: CARS-MODE scores 0.04218, 6.22\% above NSGA-II with returned-population repair. The reference audit, however, finds 2281 lower-bound-clipped coordinates among 68248 front points. Under unclipped analytic feasible envelopes and reference point 1.05, CARS-MODE scores 0.00043362 versus 0.00043374 for NSGA-II with repair and ranks fourth overall; common-reference IGD+ ranks it fifth. The fixed-parameter, single-strategy control also remains ahead, so adaptation is unresolved. An archived composition-level AC check remains illustrative rather than seed-replicated: CARS-MODE is feasible in 0.611 of cases versus 0.500 without planning and 0.667 for NSGA-II. Thus the original external-control advantage is normalization-sensitive. The supported contribution is a reproducible constrained-search and diagnostic workflow, not consistent optimizer or electrical superiority.
